lines.trans: My son graduated from Seoul National University and just joined KBS.
Please give me five green-tea pancakes and five plain pancakes.
Seung-chan, why are you standing out here?
You could have sent a subordinate, yet you came out to buy them yourself—how admirable!
I am the very lowest junior on the team.
Did you call to tell me to return the umbrella?
It looks like today's late fee will come out of my salary.
Fine, I will give you back the umbrella and pay you the late fee too.
Could you possibly hand it over right now?
No way. I am in the middle of stage rehearsals right now.
Great, I will be right over!

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
Did you hear about this son?
I was busy today because of son.
Let's graduated and together today.
I worked hard to graduated and yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this green tea?
I was busy today because of green tea.
Did you hear about this sweet filled pancakes?
I was busy today because of sweet filled pancakes.
There are five here.
Altogether, it is five people.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this subordinate, junior?
I was busy today because of subordinate, junior.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
I understand well (going out of your way).
Today is a (going out of your way) busy day.

meanings.note: Indicates doing something personally without an intermediary.

examples.trans: Did you make this cake yourself?
Let's meet in person tomorrow and talk.

meanings.note: Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: superlative adverb placed before an adjective or adverb

examples.text: 한국 음식 중에서 비빔밥을 제일 좋아해요.
examples.trans: Among Korean foods, I like bibimbap the most.

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.
I'll call right now.
Did you hear about this today's share?
I was busy today because of today's share.

I was busy today because of late fee.

examples.trans: I received my salary.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: Since it's raining, please use an umbrella.
I lost my umbrella.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: physical performance stage
a musical or show performance on stage

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
Today's stage performance was really great.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'rehearsal', commonly used in broadcasting and performing arts.

examples.trans: There is a rehearsal before the performance.
The rehearsal starts at 2 p.m.

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
